transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Patel (CTO, BrightHarbor), Mark Reynolds (Sr. Infra Eng), Jamal Brooks (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick status, canary numbers, kernel rollback discussed, security trusts requested, runbook agreed.

Topics covered: canary metrics, fallback routing incident, kernel quant rollback vs new kernel, KV cache warmup, telemetry export limitations, KMS questions.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Sophie Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna kick off, quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:06] Dr. Aisha Patel: yeah loud and clear Sophie thanks.
[00:09] Mark Reynolds: yep, good here. Jamal's on as well.
[00:12] Jamal Brooks: hey all, sorry late on a pager but i'm here.
[00:18] Miguel Alvarez: morning — Miguel from Redwood, i'll jump into the traffic graphs and the kernel notes.
[00:22] Sophie Park: awesome. quick agenda: review the week 9 canary numbers, talk through the fallback that happened on 02/26, decide kernel plan (upgrade or roll back), and action items. any additions?
[00:31] Mark Reynolds: i'd like to add the egress encryption question — our security team wants more detail on KMS and key isolation for on-prem.
[00:36] Sophie Park: good call, we'll cover it.

[00:45] Miguel Alvarez: ok, jumping into canary. last week we ran a 20% shard to the new kernel+quant profile. p50 was stable at 48ms, p95 about 210ms, p99 spiked to 1.1s during a small garbage-collection-ish event — we think it correlates with KV cache cold start. i have the heatmap in the shared sheet. note the latency tail is mostly on long context replays.
[01:12] Mark Reynolds: that aligns with our infra capture — i see a burst on node bh-onprem-03 around 03:18 UTC where the KV cache didn't warm up quickly.
[01:20] Jamal Brooks: yeah we saw that — also a misconfigured iptables rule caused a small reconnect loop that amplified the tail. we've since tightened it.

[01:30] Sophie Park: the fallback that triggered on 02/26 — can you walk us through that? i know it hit a model-variant fallback and then region fallback.
[01:38] Miguel Alvarez: sure, so the policy was: if p95 > 300ms or error rate > 1% for one minute then fallback to a lower-quant model variant. at 03:17 the node reported a 4% increase in 5xx due to open file descriptors exhaustion from that reconnect loop. routing kicked in, traffic moved to the fallback pool but some sessions kept trying direct and hit a K/V mismatch leading to short-lived errors; Redwood's canary detected and rerouted again.
[02:05] Dr. Aisha Patel: some of our clinicians saw a delay, which is not acceptable during the triage flow. is there a way to make fallback seamless?
[02:12] Miguel Alvarez: two levers: prefix KV caching (keep warm the active conversation prefixes) and tighter circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid oscillation. we can also enable sticky routing for critical sessions to keep them on the original pool until the session completes. but sticky routing increases blast radius.
[02:33] Mark Reynolds: sticky routing is tricky for us because of multi-az failovers. if an AZ goes down we need routing to failover automatically.
[02:40] Miguel Alvarez: understoood — we can do session affinity with fallback override: prefer affinity but allow forced failover for health events. it's a config swap not a code change.

[02:52] Jamal Brooks: can we talk about KV cache TTLs? our workload has many short-lived docs and warmup is costly.
[02:58] Miguel Alvarez: yep, we're seeing a lot of cold start penalties in the heatmap. suggestions: increase async prefetch for known prefixes, longer soft TTL during peak windows, and a small local in-memory prewarm cache on the host — that reduces round trips. there's also an experimental prefix-join optimization in our runtime (labelled pq-join) but it's plumbing-level and we need to validate.
[03:25] Dr. Aisha Patel: will that impact correctness? we need to ensure no stale data returned for patient notes.
[03:30] Miguel Alvarez: correctness maintained — prefix prefetches are read-only copies, TTL controls validity. we can also pin critical prefixes to be non-evictable.

[03:40] Sophie Park: switching to kernel topic — Miguel you recommended a rollback after the 02/26 incident? pros/cons?
[03:47] Miguel Alvarez: yes. the new kernel (5.x-redwood-qa) improved throughput but introduces a rare page-swap stall on certain CPU microcode. It's low frequency but high impact (tail). rollback to 5.x-stable removes that tail at the cost of ~6% throughput. trade-off: if you prioritize latency tails (clinician UX) rollback now. if you need throughput for batch inference, keep and isolate.
[04:12] Mark Reynolds: given our SLA we can't accept 1.1s tail for interactive triage. we'd prefer rollback for the prod pool and keep the new kernel in a dedicated experimental pool.
[04:21] Sophie Park: ok decision tentatively rollback on prod; keep new kernel in the experimental island. Miguel can you run a perf job on bh-onprem-03 and confirm rollback baseline numbers?
[04:29] Miguel Alvarez: yea i'll run the flamegraphs and perf counters, also capture eBPF trace, and upload.

[04:35] Jamal Brooks: what's the rollback playbook? is it manual or can we patch through the control plane?
[04:39] Miguel Alvarez: we have an automated rollback flow in the private control plane: flag the pool and it does a canary rollback with graceful drains. we'll share the runbook. add on that, we recommend a 30-minute canary with traffic ramping at 10% increments.

[04:52] Dr. Aisha Patel: security: KMS/HSM integration, how isolated are keys for the on-prem package? and do you persist any plaintext tokens?
[04:59] Sophie Park: quick answer — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys. we don't persist plaintext model inputs or tokens in the control plane; audit logs only show token hashes and request metadata. we'll send the SOC2 excerpts and KMS integration note after this call.
[05:15] Mark Reynolds: also need clarity on SSO/SAML user roles for the console — our auditors require RBAC screenshots.
[05:20] Sophie Park: noted, i'll include console RBAC docs.

[05:27] Miguel Alvarez: regarding telemetry — we noticed a retention gap for on-prem: only 14 days for token-level traces currently, whereas you asked for 90 days. options: ship to your SIEM (recommended) or extend local retention (disk costs). shipping to your collector with structured JSON events is straightforward; we'll provide a sample FluentBit/Logstash config.
[05:50] Jamal Brooks: we'll prefer ship-to-SIEM for compliance, please share the sample config.

[06:00] Sophie Park: ok wrapping toward next steps. to recap: BrightHarbor requests prod rollback to 5.x-stable this week, runway canary 30m, Redwood to run perf tests and upload traces, and security docs to be shared by Friday.
[06:12] Mark Reynolds: timeline: if we get the docs and rollback plan by Friday, infra will schedule the rollback Saturday maintenance window.
[06:18] Dr. Aisha Patel: please make sure clinicians are warned — Jamal will coordinate internal comms.

[06:24] Miguel Alvarez: i'll also enable tighter circuit-breaker thresholds for the prod pool to reduce oscillation and push a config to disable model-variant sticky for non-critical sessions.
[06:33] Jamal Brooks: noted. i will validate the new egress ACLs and send a topology map.

[06:40] Sophie Park: cool, any outstanding questions?
[06:43] Dr. Aisha Patel: one — is there an ETA on the pq-join optimization? we might be able to test it in the exp pool.
[06:50] Miguel Alvarez: it's experimental, early April at best. we can include you in the early test cohort if you want.
[06:56] Mark Reynolds: sign us up, we'll run in exp pool only.

[07:00] Sophie Park: perfect. i'll follow up with updated notes and the SOC2 + KMS doc. Miguel, you run the perf, Mark and Jamal will share topology and ACLs. we'll reconvene next Tuesday to review the rollback post-canary.
[07:12] Miguel Alvarez: thanks everyone, i'll post flamegraphs and the perf job links.
[07:15] Jamal Brooks: thanks, bye.
[07:17] Dr. Aisha Patel: thanks all.

(Transcript ends)
